label: late original-phase n (or h/l/o/f/v/r) after several v/c/y/t/a/q/m/u inputs
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at t<2, at the delimiter, or during copy. Rate rises with position (lift about 9x at orig_idx 7-8) and is highest on the last few inputs before <DEL>. The input token matters most: n carries half the activation mass (11x lift) and all of the top activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max). h, l, o, f, v and r give weaker activations. Strength also depends on history: it is higher when earlier inputs include v, c, y, t, a, q, m or u (first_tok t/y and prev_tok v/c each lift about 3x), so it looks like a graded sum of input-token identity and an accumulated-context direction rather than a crisp rule. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (85% of mass). n alone on dev gives P 0.37 and R 0.34. The two-clause history predicate reaches F1 about 0.50 and mass recall 0.66, which leaves many weak activations on other tokens unexplained.
